title: Copilot Studio: service principal as owner of workflows
summary: The roadmap facts, workflow capacity description and application-user API are supported. No blocking errors were found; minor corrections concern the application-user path ending early and checklist controls missing from the table.

claims.quote: Workflows can now be owned under a service principal (a Microsoft Entra app registration) instead of a named user account.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe service principal ownership of Copilot Studio workflows.

claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio workflows service principal default owner API'; checked roadmap, workflows overview, FAQ and designer. None states what happens to ownership on arrival.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn does not establish that these Copilot Studio workflows use application users or Power Automate's service principal flow model.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio workflows service principal license capacity rate application user'; read workflow FAQ, application-user management and Power Automate support. Power Automate flow ownership is documented, but not ownership of these workflows.

claims.claim: The role permitted to assign a service principal workflow owner and its required permissions are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio workflows service principal roles assign connections'; read workflows overview, FAQ and designer. No role for assigning a service principal workflow owner was found.

claims.claim: Feature-specific prerequisites, including whether the owner must already be an application user in the environment, are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio workflow service principal license capacity rate application user'; read workflows FAQ and overview, application-user management and Power Automate support. No prerequisite specific to this ownership option found.

claims.claim: The execution and connection identity implications of service principal workflow ownership are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio workflows service principal roles assign connections'; read overview, FAQ and designer. Search found a Copilot-node connected-user description, but no service-principal-owner runtime or connection identity rule.

claims.claim: Workflows have a consumption model, consuming Copilot Studio capacity for each action executed.
claims.quote: Workflows consume Copilot Studio capacity for each action they execute.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating reflects metered workflow capacity consumption.
claims.quote: Workflows consume Copilot Studio capacity for each action they execute.

claims.claim: Executed workflow actions are a unit of capacity-consuming activity.
claims.quote: Workflows consume Copilot Studio capacity for each action they execute.

claims.claim: The workflows FAQ says the harness uses usage-based billing.

claims.claim: Using, building, testing and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Using, building, testing, and evaluating agents might consume Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Power Automate already supports service principal application users owning and running flows.
claims.quote: Power Automate supports service principal application users owning and running flows.

claims.claim: Power Automate documents licensing implications for service principal application users.
claims.quote: Since a service principal application user is a non-interactive user without a user license, it's subject to non-licensed user limits and has special licensing and request limit implications.

claims.claim: Workflow connector actions can reach Microsoft 365 services, third-party services and custom connectors to perform tasks and retrieve data.
claims.quote: Connectors: Connect to various services to perform tasks and retrieve data. Connectors include Microsoft 365 services, third-party services, and custom connectors.

claims.claim: An application user can be created as an unlicensed user in an environment.
claims.quote: You can create an unlicensed application user in your environment.

claims.claim: The application-user UI lets the administrator select security roles for a new application user.
claims.quote: Select the edit icon to select security roles for the new application user. After adding security roles, select Save.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users reaches the application-user list.
claims.quote: Select Manage in the navigation pane. In the Manage pane, select Environments. Then select an environment. Select Settings. Select Users + permissions, and then select Application users.
claims.fix: The path correctly reaches the list but stops before choosing an app registration. For controls[1].ui.path use 'Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Users + permissions > Application users > + New app user > + Add an app', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-application-users. Keep the existing shorter route in inventory advice.

claims.claim: The printed POST addAppUser endpoint and api-version=2020-10-01 create an application user in the target environment.
claims.quote: POST https://api.bap.microsoft.com/providers/Microsoft.BusinessAppPlatform/scopes/admin/environments/{environmentIdGuid}/addAppUser?api-version=2020-10-01

claims.claim: The create application-user endpoint is documented as preview.
claims.quote:
Create a Dataverse application user (preview)
[This article is pre-release documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.claim: The create endpoint request body identifies the app registration through servicePrincipalAppId.
Callers must be Power Platform administrators or a Power Platform Service Principal application.
claims.quote: Callers of this endpoint must either be Power Platform administrators or a Power Platform Service Principal application.

claims.claim: The endpoint always adds the application user as a System Administrator.
claims.quote: This always adds the application user as a System Administrator.

claims.where: controls[1].governs and scope; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Application users represent app registrations in an environment.
claims.quote: On the Application users page, you can view and manage application users. The Custom app type is your local app registration, as created in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Application-user security roles can be reviewed and edited on the Application users page.
claims.quote: You can select Edit security roles on the menu bar on the Application users page. If the application user has roles assigned already, those roles appear as selected on the page.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Application users can be deactivated.
claims.quote: To deactivate an application user, select Deactivate on the menu bar, and then select Deactivate in the confirmation dialog.

claims.claim: The application-user page documents deleting application users.
claims.quote:
Delete an inactive, application user
Only application users with the inactive state can be deleted.

claims.claim: An enabled workflow starts new runs when its trigger fires on a schedule, connector event or agent call.
claims.quote: When a workflow is enabled, its trigger is active, so a new run starts whenever the trigger fires: on schedule, on a connector event, or when an agent calls it.

claims.claim: The Workflows page has an Enabled column showing whether each workflow is enabled.
claims.quote:
Use the Workflows page to review and manage your workflows.
The Enabled column shows whether a workflow is enabled.

claims.claim: The Workflows page has a Credit usage (last 30 days) column showing credits consumed by a workflow.
claims.quote: The Credit usage (last 30 days) column shows the credits that a workflow consumed during the last 30 days.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio is the documented route to review Agent flow actions used by each workflow.
claims.quote: In the Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio, review the Agent flow actions used by each workflow.

claims.where: Change & support; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The workflow overview says new runs are blocked once the environment's prepaid capacity is consumed, until capacity is available.
claims.quote: Once you fully consume your environment's prepaid Copilot Studio capacity, new workflow runs are blocked until capacity is available.

claims.claim: Already running workflows complete normally when prepaid capacity is consumed.
claims.quote: Running workflows complete normally.

claims.claim: Learn suggests pay-as-you-go billing to avoid workflow interruption.
claims.quote: To avoid interruption, monitor capacity usage and consider turning on pay-as-you-go billing.
